chunk.title: Project: FlowSense - Technical Implementation
chunk.content:
Project Name: FlowSense
Technical Details:
Implemented in Python with FastAPI, FlowSense sits as a reverse proxy in front of LLM providers. Semantic caching uses SentenceTransformers embeddings stored in Redis to evaluate prompt similarity, serving cached completions for high-frequency queries in under 20ms and cutting API token spend. Security guardrails use Qdrant vector search coupled with regex rules to detect prompt injections, jailbreak patterns, and PII leaks before requests hit upstream models. An embedded DeBERTa model performs real-time output grounding to detect hallucinations against retrieved context, and an automated complexity router routes simple queries to cost-efficient models (like Claude 3.5 Haiku) and difficult prompts to frontier models.
Architecture Details:
High-throughput asynchronous proxy pipeline. Incoming requests pass through security interception, semantic cache lookup, dynamic complexity routing, upstream execution, and response grounding analysis before returning to the client, with cryptographically signed logs stored in a SOC2-ready vault.
Stack Details:
Languages: Python, Bash
Frameworks: FastAPI, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers
Databases: Redis, Qdrant (Vector DB)
APIs: OpenAI-Compatible REST API, Anthropic API, Gemini API
Auth: Bearer Tokens, API Key Gateway Management
Deployment: Docker, Kubernetes-ready, Linux
Design Patterns: Reverse Proxy, Decorator Pattern, Chain of Responsibility, Semantic Cache Pattern
Libraries: sentence-transformers, qdrant-client, redis, fastapi, uvicorn, transformers, torch
AI Models: SentenceTransformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), DeBERTa-v3 Hallucination Classifier, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Haiku

chunk.title: Project: FlowSense - FAQ: How does FlowSense achieve sub-20ms semantic cache responses?
chunk.content:
Project: FlowSense
Question: How does FlowSense achieve sub-20ms semantic cache responses?
Answer: FlowSense computes vector embeddings of incoming prompts and queries a high-speed Redis index using cosine similarity thresholds. Exact or near-identical prompts are served immediately from Redis without calling upstream LLM APIs.

chunk.title: Project: FlowSense - FAQ: How does the complexity router decide where to send prompts?
chunk.content:
Project: FlowSense
Question: How does the complexity router decide where to send prompts?
Answer: The gateway analyzes token length, syntactic depth, reasoning keywords, and multi-turn context. Straightforward conversational queries are dispatched to lightweight models like Claude 3.5 Haiku, while complex coding or reasoning prompts are routed to frontier models like GPT-4o, reducing operational costs by up to 60%.

chunk.title: Project: Parity - Summary
chunk.content:
Project Name: Parity
Tagline: Parity is a deterministic-first Oracle to PostgreSQL SQL & PL/SQL migration and transpilation engine with a 5-layer mathematical verification stack and zero raw data leakage.
Recruiter Explanation:
Parity demonstrates Cimil's deep mastery of compilers, language engineering, and formal verification. Rather than relying on non-deterministic LLMs that produce silent semantic errors in enterprise database migrations (such as Oracle null-string equivalence or outer join semantics), Cimil built an AST-driven rewrite engine verified by 5 mathematical layers—syntax parsing, type schema parity, relational algebra, differential symbolic execution, and automated GitHub PR creation. The system achieves a 94% verified pass rate on a 500-object enterprise benchmark.
Languages: Python, SQL, PL/SQL
Frameworks: sqlglot, ANTLR, FastAPI, Pydantic
Databases: PostgreSQL, Oracle

chunk.title: Project: Parity - Technical Implementation
chunk.content:
Project Name: Parity
Technical Details:
The core transpiler operates on Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) using sqlglot and custom dialect rules to map Oracle SQL and PL/SQL semantics to ANSI/PostgreSQL equivalents. Transpiled code is verified across 5 distinct layers: Layer 1 checks syntactic validity and grammar via dual-engine AST parsing. Layer 2 verifies type system and schema parity against target catalog definitions. Layer 3 proves relational algebra equivalence. Layer 4 performs differential symbolic execution with zero raw data leakage to guarantee identical runtime behavior on edge-case semantics (e.g. ORA_DIFF_001 null handling, string concatenation, outer joins, and ROWNUM evaluation order). Layer 5 integrates with GitHub Actions to emit automated migration PRs.
Architecture Details:
Deterministic-first modular compiler architecture. Separation of the syntax transformation stage from the mathematical verification pipeline. The verification pipeline acts as an immutable gatekeeper: candidate queries are proposed by either rewrite rules or constrained LLMs, but are only accepted if all 5 verification layers mathematically certify semantic equivalence.
Stack Details:
Languages: Python, SQL, PL/SQL
Frameworks: sqlglot, ANTLR, FastAPI, Pydantic
Databases: PostgreSQL, Oracle
APIs: GitHub REST API, CLI
Auth: API Keys, GitHub App Tokens
Deployment: Docker, GitHub Actions, CLI
Design Patterns: Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) Visitor, Pipeline Pattern, Formal Verification Gatekeeper, Differential Execution
Libraries: sqlglot, pydantic, pytest, z3-solver
AI Models: Constrained LLM Transpilation Fallback with Mathematical Verification Gate

chunk.title: Project: Parity - FAQ: Why can't generic LLMs reliably migrate Oracle SQL to PostgreSQL?
chunk.content:
Project: Parity
Question: Why can't generic LLMs reliably migrate Oracle SQL to PostgreSQL?
Answer: Generic LLMs only ensure syntactic validity; they frequently fail silently on runtime semantics such as Oracle treating empty strings as NULL, string concatenation with NULL, legacy (+) outer joins, and ROWNUM execution order. Parity uses a 5-layer verification stack that mathematically checks relational algebra and differential symbolic execution before approving any migration.

chunk.title: Project: Parity - FAQ: What benchmark was used to validate Parity?
chunk.content:
Project: Parity
Question: What benchmark was used to validate Parity?
Answer: Parity was evaluated against an enterprise benchmark of 500 diverse Oracle SQL and PL/SQL objects spanning base queries, legacy outer joins, complex analytic functions, subqueries, and PL/SQL blocks, achieving an overall verified pass rate of 94%.

This project showcases Cimil's capability at the intersection of Computer Vision, Edge AI, Industrial IoT, and Distributed Systems. Built on real-world industrial datasets, the system handles supervised defect classification, unsupervised anomaly detection for never-before-seen defects, explainable AI with Grad-CAM, and privacy-preserving federated model updates across simulated factories—demonstrating production-grade ML engineering.

chunk.title: Project: Secure AI Quality Inspector - Technical Implementation
chunk.content:
Project Name: Secure AI Quality Inspector
Technical Details:
The architecture ingests camera images through an AES-256-GCM encrypted transport channel with SHA-256 integrity verification. Preprocessing applies CLAHE contrast optimization and bilateral denoising. A dual-model vision pipeline executes in parallel: a fine-tuned YOLOv8m model classifies known defects across 4 verified categories, while a PatchCore memory-bank model detects novel zero-shot structural anomalies. Predictions are visually explained with Grad-CAM activation heatmaps. The system computes severity metrics and estimated scrap cost in Indian Rupees (₹). A 3-node federated learning simulation using FedAvg trains models collaboratively across simulated factory nodes without centralizing raw fabric imagery.
Architecture Details:
Edge-to-cloud industrial inspection architecture. Client edge cameras transmit encrypted frames to a FastAPI backend. Inference outputs are served to a Streamlit operations console and stored in an encrypted database. Model updates are federated via decentralized weights aggregation.
Stack Details:
Languages: Python
Frameworks: FastAPI, Streamlit, PyTorch, Ultralytics YOLOv8
Databases: SQLite, File System Object Store
APIs: FastAPI REST Endpoints, Edge WebSocket Stream
Auth: JWT, Role-Based Access (Admin / Quality Operator)
Deployment: Docker, Edge Device / Local Server

chunk.title: Project: Secure AI Quality Inspector - FAQ: Why combine YOLOv8 with PatchCore?
chunk.content:
Project: Secure AI Quality Inspector
Question: Why combine YOLOv8 with PatchCore?
Answer: YOLOv8 excels at rapidly localizing and classifying known, labeled defect classes. However, in manufacturing, novel or unseen defects can occur. PatchCore uses a memory bank of normal visual features to flag any abnormal deviations without needing prior training examples of that specific defect.

chunk.title: Project: Secure AI Quality Inspector - FAQ: How does the federated learning component work?
chunk.content:
Project: Secure AI Quality Inspector
Question: How does the federated learning component work?
Answer: A 3-node FedAvg architecture trains local models on private factory image batches, sending only gradient updates to a coordinator node that aggregates weights, preserving proprietary factory imagery and maintaining privacy.

chunk.title: Project: VendorIQ - Technical Implementation
chunk.content:
Project Name: VendorIQ
Technical Details:
The backend is implemented in Python using FastAPI, structured into modules for Auth, Vendor CRUD, Scenario Management, and a specialized Decision Intelligence engine. The engine processes multi-criteria vendor metrics through Weighted Sum Models and TOPSIS algorithms. Data persistence is managed via PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy ORM and Alembic migrations, while Redis is utilized for caching and performance optimization. The API follows a RESTful pattern, secured via JWT-based authentication with role-based access control (RBAC).
Architecture Details:
The project utilizes a three-tier modular monolithic architecture. The Presentation Layer is a Next.js application that communicates over a REST API with the Application Layer. The Application Layer is modularized by business domain (Auth, Vendors, Scenarios), ensuring separation of concerns while allowing for shared access to the decision engine components.
Stack Details:

Frameworks: FastAPI, Next.js, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, React

Deployment: Render, Docker

chunk.content:
Project: VendorIQ
Question: What is the core purpose of the decision engine?
Answer: The decision engine allows procurement teams to quantify qualitative and quantitative vendor data using mathematical models like TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) to rank vendors according to specific weighted criteria.

chunk.title: Project: VendorIQ - FAQ: How does the project handle scaling of metrics?
chunk.content:
Project: VendorIQ
Question: How does the project handle scaling of metrics?
Answer: The project uses SQL subqueries to fetch the latest metrics for vendors, ensuring that decision calculations are always based on the most recent data point available in the PostgreSQL database.
